metadata.title: World Digest — October 29, 2026
metadata.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro fled to Miami after declaring himself Brazil's rightful president-elect, while Spain reeled from its second deadly rail crash this year with at least 68 killed. Wall Street opened lower as Alphabet's results stoked AI spending fears and WTI crude surged to $102.78.

sections.title: Political News
sections.content:
Americas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth forced out another top Pentagon general, this time the Joint Staff’s top military planner, amid accusations of leaking classified information on Iran and Ukraine The Washington Post CBS News. The purge follows a reported Chinese spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, with a businesswoman allegedly passing intelligence to Beijing The New York Times. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro, declaring himself Brazil’s rightful president-elect, fled to Miami after leaving Brazil Reuters. With GOP midterm hopes slipping, tech, crypto, and industrial firms are rushing to K Street to hedge against a possible Democratic takeover of Congress Politico.

Europe

Spain’s second major rail crash this year killed at least 68 people, with investigators focusing on train traffic controllers’ roles NBC News. ECB President Christine Lagarde announced her early resignation, with two pragmatists leading the race to replace her CNBC. In the UK, Chancellor John Healey accepted a smaller fiscal buffer after global shocks hit the economy Reuters. Russell Brand denied all charges as he testified at his rape and sexual assault trial, saying sex was consensual AP News. Europe’s youth are protesting, feeling locked out of the future BBC.

Asia-Pacific

Hong Kong leader John Lee apologized for a deadly high-rise fire, blaming the construction industry, while the housing minister resigned Reuters. China’s Communist Party expelled a record 33 officials in a purge as Xi emphasized “party discipline” BBC. North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles as tensions with the South intensified over a landmine blast Al Jazeera. The U.S., UK, Canada, and EU sanctioned a North Korean network accused of infiltrating U.S. companies Fox Business. Real Madrid apologized to China over Kylian Mbappé’s Mao “dictator” comment ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos.

Middle East & Africa

A ship was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran faced pressure to make nuclear concessions amid looming strikes Axios CBS News. Putin sought to expand ties with African leaders at a Moscow summit AP News.

sections.title: Financial News
sections.content:
Global Markets Rattled by AI Spending Fears, Fed Holds Rates

US Equities & Economy Nasdaq futures fell 1% as Alphabet’s results intensified concerns over AI capital expenditure Reuters. Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq were set to open lower after Caterpillar and Alphabet earnings, while inflation data met expectations Reuters. Caterpillar shares slumped on a revenue miss and unchanged growth target, digging a hole for the Dow Investor's Business Daily. The Federal Reserve left rates steady, with Governor Lisa Cook dissenting; commentators warn the pause risks playing catch-up on inflation Axios. The Fed's favored inflation gauge trended higher in September, suggesting a tightening path Reuters.

Corporate News Weil, Gotshal & Manges, a longtime Wall Street law firm, plans to dissolve, capping a dizzying fall CNBC. Eli Lilly profits surged on weight-loss drug demand, blowing past estimates and hiking its sales outlook Financial Times. DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion in a major grocery-delivery consolidation AP News. ServiceNow stock plunged 19% on slower contract growth, while Oracle popped 11% on a plan to turn cash flow positive by 2028 Yahoo Finance Barron's. Volkswagen posted its largest loss in over a decade due to a Porsche writedown and China woes The New York Times.

Other Headlines The FTC ordered Delta, Uber, and others to hand over data on algorithmic pricing The Guardian. US Health Secretary RFK Jr. will expand access to unapproved peptides BBC. Nvidia's CEO is reportedly a target of a Chinese spy plot The New York Times. SK Hynix stock jumped on a blockbuster Q3 earnings beat, with profit surging 632% Investor's Business Daily.

sections.title: Entertainment News
sections.content:
Film

Barbara Barrie, the Tony-winning actress best known as the mother in Breaking Away, died at 95. Los Angeles Times

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping drew early praise, with Elle Fanning’s style hailed as her "Effie Trinket era." The Hollywood Reporter

Alexander Payne was hit with a copyright suit over The Holdovers script. Variety

Wildwood is getting a 4K Steelbook edition; the stop-motion film has sparked a box-office comeback for Laika. IGN

Cate Blanchett warned against "unthinking certainty" while accepting Japan’s Praemium Imperiale. The Hollywood Reporter

Walter Koenig, Chekov on the original Star Trek, died at 90; William Shatner said he was "deeply saddened." The Hollywood Reporter

TV & Streaming

Russell Brand took the stand at his rape trial, where his wife called him a "wonderful father." BBC

Hayden Panettiere’s death was ruled accidental, closing the police investigation. NBC News

Smile 3 set David Bruckner to direct, while creator Parker Finn helms a Possession remake. Variety

Cynthia Erivo called public "annoyance" over her Ariana Grande friendship a double-edged sword. Variety

South Park tackled America’s beef shortage with a "GTA VI" sneak peek. The Guardian

Matthew Perry’s sister remembered him three years after his death amid a new docuseries. ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

Industry

Tyler Perry fought to keep private texts confidential in a $77M assault lawsuit. TMZ

Skydance TV’s George Cheeks revealed the executive structure following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger. Variety

WWE moved Crown Jewel to a new Riyadh venue amid Middle East tensions. Forbes

Paris Jackson called the Michael Jackson estate executor’s $109M fee request "offensive." Rolling Stone

sections.title: Stock Analysis
sections.content:
IPOs

The IPO calendar remains active. On 2026-10-29, Georgia Banking Company (GBC) is set to list on the Nasdaq Yahoo Finance. Two days later, on 2026-10-30, OPay Limited (OPAY) will debut on the NYSE, and Deep Sea Minerals Corp. (SEAM) on the Nasdaq Yahoo Finance Yahoo Finance. Recent pricings include MSG Rangers Corp. (MSGR) on the NYSE (2026-10-27) and Gunnison Copper Corp. (GUNN) on the NYSE American (2026-10-26) Yahoo Finance Yahoo Finance.

Major Indices

The S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98, while the Dow gained 0.19% to 52,475.10 Yahoo Finance. The Nasdaq added 0.27% to 26,549.85, and the small-cap Russell 2000 outperformed, up 0.41% to 2,830.51 Yahoo Finance. The VIX fell 3.48% to 16.91, indicating easing volatility Yahoo Finance.

Sectors

Technology led gains, advancing 0.80%, followed by Financials (0.45%) and Energy (0.35%) Yahoo Finance. On the downside, Utilities slumped 0.84%, Real Estate fell 0.73%, and Communication Services dropped 0.42% Yahoo Finance. Consumer Staples also lagged, down 0.36%.

Major Stocks

Broadcom jumped 2.77% to $351.81, with Alphabet up 1.34% and JPMorgan gaining 1.05% Yahoo Finance. Amazon rose 0.59% Yahoo Finance. Conversely, Meta fell 1.24%, Nvidia dropped 1.17%, and Apple declined 0.94% Yahoo Finance. Tesla lost 0.80%, while Microsoft was nearly flat (-0.06%) Yahoo Finance.

Notable Movers

No individual gainers/losers beyond the major stocks were provided. Broadcom’s 2.77% advance and Meta’s 1.24% decline were the standout moves among large caps Yahoo Finance.

Rates & Commodities

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 1.04% to 5.05%, a notable level Yahoo Finance. WTI crude oil surged 2.88% to $102.78, a significant one-day move Yahoo Finance. Gold slipped 0.56% to $4,051.60, while Bitcoin edged up 0.57% to $81,267.59 Yahoo Finance.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.content:
Next 24–48 Hours - Markets on edge: Nasdaq futures fell on AI capex fears after Alphabet; Caterpillar's miss adds downside risk. Watch for follow-through selling in tech and industrials. The Fed's hawkish hold, with Governor Cook dissenting, keeps rate policy front and center. - Geopolitical flashpoints: A burning ship in the Strait of Hormuz and mounting pressure on Iran over nuclear concessions could spike oil further—WTI already surged past $102. North Korea's missile salvo may escalate after the landmine incident.

Next Week - IPO wave: OPay (OPAY) and Deep Sea Minerals (SEAM) debut Oct 30; Georgia Banking (GBC) lists today. Weak reception would signal risk-off sentiment. - China purge aftermath: Record expulsions signal tightening party discipline; watch for follow-on policy signals affecting foreign business.

Next Month - Bolsonaro’s Miami flight could destabilize Brazilian politics, with possible market volatility ahead. - Lagarde’s early exit sets up a leadership race; a pragmatist successor may shift ECB policy direction. - US midterm hedging: K Street spending suggests investors expect a possible Democratic Congress—policy risk rising.

Key Uncertainties - Whether the Pentagon purge slows military decision-making during Iran tensions. - Whether AI capex slowdown fears deepen into a broader tech correction.

theme.name: Twin Fault Lines
theme.note: A day split between political upheaval and market tremors — two fractures running through the same page.
